61160.etyen:
ti (“ten”) + øre (“øre”) + -ing (“noun-forming suffix”), literally “ten-øre coin”.
The first element ti is from Old Norse tíu (“ten”), from Proto-Germanic *tehun (“ten”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *déḱm̥ (“ten”), whose deeper origin is uncertain. The second element øre is from Old Norse eyrir (“øre”), borrowed from Latin aureus (“gold coin”), from aurum (“gold”), from Proto-Italic *auzom (“gold”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ews- (“to dawn, become light”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk tiøring, Swedish tioöring and historical Danish tiøring (“ten-øre coin”).

1005032.etyen:
Compound of Lærdal (“municipality and district in Vestland”) + fjord (“fjord”), with linking -s- (“interfix”) and definite singular -en (“definite singular suffix”), literally “the Lærdal fjord”.
The first element Lærdal is from Middle Norwegian Lærdall, attested in 1427, from Old Norse Læradalr, probably reduced from reconstructed *Lærardalr. The latter consists of the genitive *Lærar of a lost river name *Lærr and dalr (“valley, dale”), literally “valley of the Lærr”. The origin of the river name is uncertain.
